c.tagline: Mountains, beaches, and rhythm in the air.

avoid.reason: Includes Cidade de Deus, Complexo do Alemão and much of the north and west zones. Rated "Do Not Travel" — avoid even on guided tours.
Lively by day and evening, but streets empty out late — muggings and phone theft rise once the bars close.
Copacabana and Ipanema sands are best left after sunset — opportunistic robbery is common once the crowds thin.

hood_desc: The iconic beachfront neighborhood with its sweeping crescent of sand, mosaic promenade and round-the-clock energy. Suits travelers who want the classic Rio beach scene, lively nightlife and easy access, though it is busy and touristy.

A stylish, upscale beach district made famous in song, with fashionable shops, restaurants and a beautiful beach framed by the Dois Irmaos peaks. Ideal for visitors wanting chic surroundings and vibrant seaside culture.

The most affluent and exclusive neighborhood, quieter and more refined than its neighbors, with fine dining, boutiques and a lovely beach. Best for travelers seeking upscale comfort and a calmer, polished vibe.
A bohemian hilltop district of cobbled streets, colonial mansions, artists' studios and sweeping city views. Perfect for a creative crowd wanting charm, history and an offbeat, arty atmosphere.

The historic center and Rio's raucous nightlife hub around the Lapa Arches, famed for samba clubs, live music and street parties. Great for night owls chasing music and dancing, best explored with care.
lodging: O de Casa Hostel Santa Teresa

water.note: Technically treated but old pipes mean bottled or filtered water is recommended for visitors.

transit.pay: Buy a rechargeable Jaé card (replacing the old RioCard) at metro stations to tap in on Metro, VLT, and BRT; some gates also accept contactless bank cards directly. A single Metro ride costs about R$7.90 (~$1.40).
transit.hours: Metro runs about 5am-midnight (until 1am Fri/Sat); there is no all-night rail service, so late-night travelers rely on buses or ride-hailing.
